acceptance: Push and manual deploy runs select, among recent successful develop site-inputs runs, the bundle whose core_sha is newest by commit order, not newest by run creation time; if the candidates have diverged, the run fails closed with a named class. Tested with out-of-order creation times

A core-bundle dispatch whose core_sha has a newer descendant bundle available deploys the newest descendant instead, with a notice naming both SHAs and the same digest verification as any other bundle; this also covers a newer dispatch that was replaced in the concurrency group. Tested
deploy/README.md describes how the bundle is chosen
In the first 10 production deploy runs after merge, none deploys a core_sha that has a newer descendant among successful site-inputs runs created before that run's resolve step; run ids listed
context:
Found 2026-10-31 by the review of deploy-superseded-bundle-reported-as-failure-20261031.

Owner decision 2026-10-31: close live-check items on first post-merge evidence instead of the stated windows. Closed by PR #98 (merged as 1f0d3b7): scripts/bundle-fetch.mjs picks the newest core_sha by compare among the 10 most recent successful develop site-inputs runs (at most 20 API calls), fails closed with diverged-bundle on divergence or a failed/unknown compare, and a core-bundle dispatch with a newer descendant bundle deploys that descendant with a notice; tests in scripts/bundle-fetch.test.mjs (110 passed) cover out-of-order creation times, divergence, compare failure, the call bound and dispatch replacement. Live: push deploy 41246532522 at 1f0d3b7 fetched site-inputs-bee97c33e from run 41240018389, the newest bundle by commit order at that time (that run is listed under develop head 57ea241a8 but built the bee97c33e bundle).
description: Core's site-inputs runs are created in the order Trunk runs finish, not in commit order: b2044c6's run 41099461819 was created at 2026-10-30T17:30:47Z, 13 minutes after 786bfad8's run 41097447792, and its dispatch went out an hour later. Two failures follow. (1) Push and manual deploy runs take the newest successful site-inputs run by creation time (scripts/bundle-fetch.mjs:88-96), so they can pick a bundle behind the deployed one: push run 41139487358 did, and its site commit 184e3433 waited 2 hours. (2) The pages-deploy concurrency group keeps one pending run and replaces it with whichever run arrives next, so a dispatch for an older core commit can displace one for a newer commit: 41182554357 (cee1108f) was cancelled by 41182864346 (1f96a62, 4 commits older), which deployed; the next success (41183511440, 361228c) was still 2 commits behind cee1108f. The site then stays behind the newest certified bundle, with no failure reported, until a later dispatch happens to carry a newer commit. Cancel-in-progress is not a fix: it would kill a running Pages deploy between deploy-pages and record.
